accepted_recoveries: Patch the Service targetPort to the existing named container port that resolves to 8081.
forbidden_actions: Do not change the application binary to listen on the erroneous port.
Do not expose pods with hostNetwork or hostPort.
Do not change the Service selector when it already selects the intended pods.
incident.injected_fault: The catalog Service forwards to targetPort 8080 while the selected catalog containers listen on port 8081.
observable_signals: Requests through the catalog Service fail with connection refused or HTTP 503.
EndpointSlices select ready catalog pod addresses but advertise the wrong backend port.
Direct probes to catalog pod port 8081 succeed.
preconditions: Catalog pods are ready and listen on port 8081.
The Service selector matches only the intended catalog pods.
The benchmark client can reach the Service ClusterIP.
required_evidence: Capture the Service port and targetPort.
Capture the selected pod containerPort and listening socket.
Compare failing Service probes with successful direct-pod probes.

payload.answer: The root cause of the incident was a Service targetPort mismatch: the catalog-api Service in namespace proofix-case-03 was configured with targetPort 8080, while the backend pods and nginx configuration listen on port 8081 (catalog-http). This caused connection failures through the Service. The incident was resolved by patching the Service targetPort to match the backend listening port 8081.

critical_claims.claim: The catalog-api Service was configured with targetPort 8080, mismatched with the backend pods.
The catalog-api pods listen on containerPort 8081 (named catalog-http) and are running and ready.
The nginx configuration in the catalog-nginx ConfigMap specifies listen 8081.
The catalog-api Endpoints targeted port 8080 on the pod IPs due to the Service targetPort setting.
The catalog-api Service was successfully patched to route to port 8081.
